Whitey Ford was the Yankees' ace pitcher for sixteen seasons from nineteen fifty to nineteen sixty-seven, posting one of the most successful records in postseason history and anchoring the franchise's dynasty. His two hundred thirty-six regular-season wins, unparalleled clutch pitching, and leadership in the clubhouse earned him the nickname The Chairman of the Board.

Ford won two hundred thirty-six games with the Yankees during the regular season and an additional ten in the World Series—the most postseason wins ever by a pitcher. He had a career earned run average of two point seven five and led the American League in earned run average in nineteen fifty-six with a two point four seven mark and in nineteen fifty-eight with a two point oh one mark. Ford pitched for eleven American League pennant winners and six World Series champions, an unprecedented run of success.

He started the nineteen sixty-one All-Star Game and was a six-time All-Star, commanding respect across the league. Nicknamed The Chairman of the Board for his cool leadership and mastery of the pitcher's mound in high-pressure moments, Ford retired as a Yankee and remains the franchise's all-time postseason ace. Yogi Berra was his catcher and the player Berra credits much of his success to. Mickey Mantle was his contemporary and teammate during the Yankees' nineteen fifties and sixties dominance. Mariano Rivera, a later-era Yankees closer, carried the pitching legacy forward. Ford spent his career with the Yankees franchise, where he became a legend.
